launches.title: Getcho - a local-delivery platform for high-value retail
launches.tagline: Getcho: the local retail delivery platform for high-value products
launches.body:
We're [Evandro](https://www.linkedin.com/in/evandronadal), [Jack](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnpconsidine/), and [Mike,](https://github.com/consofine) and we're building Getcho, a local retail delivery platform for high-value products. Getcho runs on top of third-party fleets, delivering $250,000 of merchandise per month.

## The problem

Merchants have embraced local / on-demand delivery—it boosts sales with urgent shoppers and is cheap, thanks to mega-fleets like DoorDash, Roadie, and Uber. But locally delivered packages are lost, misdelivered, or returned up to 10% of the time; some retail locations spend thousands of dollars each day replacing lost packages.

## The solution

Getcho prevents 95% of failed local deliveries. This saves merchants the costs associated with shipping replacements and, just as important, improves customers' perception of the merchant's brand.

By flagging GPS irregularities, using AI-assisted calls and texts to guide drivers at pick-up & drop-off, and scheduling around customer availability, Getcho ensures seamless and reliable deliveries.

## Demo

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GFxJq_xekfI>

## About us

Jack and Evandro ("Dro") met in college. They started a software development firm called K-Optional that they ran for seven years. Mike, Jack's brother, joined K-Optional in 2021.

There they built logistics products that were acquired or continue to generate millions in revenue, including:

* A [pig tracking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigging) platform that uses hardware and GPS data to check diagnostics on massive oil pipelines.
* A scheduling platform in the catastrophe insurance space that maps claimants to appraisal locations.

They spun Getcho out of a curbside pick-up application and went all in once they had delivered a million dollars of merchandise.

## Ask

If you or someone you know is in retail operations, we'd love to connect & chat.

launches.title: Metreecs - AI-Powered Demand Forecasting For Retailers
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Metreecs helps retailers plan, buy, and allocate products using AI-demand forecasting. We prevent overstock and out-of-stock situations, allowing clients to eliminate waste, free up capital, and drive higher sales.

### **Problem 📉**

* **Financial Loss**: Retailers worldwide lose over $1.8 trillion annually due to poor inventory planning. This issue stems primarily from two main problems: overstock and out-of-stock.
* **Outdated Practices**: Retailers rely on outdated tools like Excel, causing inefficiencies, forecasting errors, and missed opportunities.
* **Environmental Cost**: Fashion is the 3rd most polluting industry due to massive overproduction: 73% of textiles are burned or landfilled which contributes to 900 million tons of CO2 annually.

In the world of retail, inventory planning can often feel like a guessing game. One of our prospects, a company with a whopping $250M in revenue, humorously encapsulated this challenge during a recent call:

> **_I quickly review our data and then check my crystal ball to pull a number out of thin air._**

This playful take highlights a serious issue: without the right tools for accurate demand forecasting, retail planners resort to guesswork.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=85641&key=user_uploads/1951235/e07d224f-ffef-470b-9a82-2a12ad344d58)

### **Solution 📈**

Metreecs is an **AI demand forecasting software for retailers**. We analyze large sets of internal and external data to predict consumer demand. This helps our clients align their inventory with actual market trends, reducing overproduction, stockouts, and markdowns, all while automating 90% of manual tasks.

Our demand forecasting models drive 3 different modules:

* **Buying:** We ensure that our clients buy the right products, in the right quantities for the right locations.
* **Reordering:** We anticipate stockouts before they occur, and suggest product replenishments to prevent them.
* **Rebalancing:** We provide inventory reallocation suggestions to eliminate waste and meet customer demand.

### **Our Team 👬**

* [**@Thibaut Pellegrin**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thibautpellegrin/) experienced the challenge firsthand—after co-founding a leather bag company and talking with industry experts, he realized there had to be a better way to manage inventory in retail.
* [**@Elie Dufeu**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/elie-dufeu-goldenberg/), a graduate from École Polytechnique in Applied Mathematics and Columbia in Data Science, developed forecasting models for financial institutions before joining Metreecs.
* [**@Martin Dimitrov**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mardimitrov/) led the international expansion of Lydia in Italy, before moving into early stage venture capital where he invested in AI and B2B SaaS startups.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=85641&key=user_uploads/1951235/1b4e5323-2dcf-4fb3-9c1a-88ca376ece07)

### **Our Ask 🫂**

If you’ve worked in retail, sold software to retailers, or have connections in the industry, we’d greatly appreciate an introduction!

Feel free to reach out at [**martin@metreecs.com**](mailto:martin@metreecs.com) or book a slot directly: [**https://calendly.com/martin-metreecs**](https://calendly.com/martin-metreecs)

launches.title: Wildcard: AEO, GEO, and AI Search for Ecommerce Brands
launches.tagline: Wildcard is the command center for agentic commerce. We help ecommerce and retail brands become the answer AI chooses.
launches.body:
**Traction:** 20+ Brands live. On average brands see a 5X increase in AI search revenue after 30 days.

**TL;DR:** [Wildcard ](https://wild-card.ai/)helps brands and retailers rank first across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Amazon Rufus/Alexa, and Walmart Sparky. We audit and action on how your brand, products, and collections show up across every AI search and shopping platform. Wildcard creates the roadmap, and our AI agents execute on it. We create the content AI looks for, including enriching the product catalog, new blogs, collection pages, outreach to publications, and even Reddit and YouTube content to close the gap. Operators can review, approve, and measure how actions tie back to revenue.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/dkdV-s-JztE>

**The Problem:** Shoppers are googling less and less. They want an experience where they can ask questions, like talking to an in-store rep. They're prompting about what to buy, the model names a few, people purchase those, and you're left relying on Meta's rising ad spend to acquire new customers or retain existing ones. Producing content for millions of SKUs is beyond human scale, and what we found is that millions in revenue was lost because of it. Below is what we learned after 7 months talking with brand owners.

**What We Learned:**

1. It's not about training the model. Everyone gets this wrong. When someone asks, the model runs a live search, reads what it finds, and picks. What decides it is boring and specific: a catalog structured so the model can trust it, and the right content on the sources it reads.
2. Existing tools were built for SaaS. They hand you a score and stop. That playbook breaks the moment you have 5,000 SKUs and variants. A brand and retailers unit of AEO is the catalog, not a homepage.

**The Solution:** Our solution is simple. First, we run a full audit of how you show up across AI search. Second, we build your roadmap. Lastly, we optimize your product catalog and create the content that gets you recommended. After 30 days, we tend to see a 5x increase in revenue.

**Our Ask:** Try a free trial of our tool [here](https://wild-card.ai/). And if you know any brands, retailers, or agencies, an intro would be great!: [kaushik@wild-card.ai](mailto:kaushik@wild-card.ai)  

**About Me:** Kaushik Mahorker (Founder & CEO). Previously, I was an Engineering Manager at Scale AI, where I led the GenAI Allocation team and built the ecommerce enrichment engine that structured 2.4M attributes across 400K SKUs, helping close $15M+ in retail and marketplace contracts.
